riddle_original: أنا لي حافظ الحومة دار بدار، وخبارك كلها عندي، وبلا بيا ما تقدر تصاوب شهادة السكنى.
riddle_english: I am the protector of the neighborhood, house by house; I have all your news, and without me, you cannot obtain a residence certificate.

riddle_original: أنا ورقة كيحلم بيها شحال من واحد، بيا الطاكسي كيخدم، ومولايا كيكريني ويشد الفلوس وهو جالس فدارو
riddle_english: I am a piece of paper that many people dream of, through me the taxi operates, and my owner rents me out and collects money while sitting at home.

riddle_original: انا لحاجة لي كايطيها لملك لناس لي برزو مزيان ف شي حاجة يا يما ف لفن، لعلم ولا ف شؤون لبلاد
riddle_english: I am a thing that the King gives to people who have excelled in something, whether in art, science, or state affairs.

riddle_original: انا لي الا بغيتي تزوج خاص ضروري تحضرني
riddle_english: I am the one that if you want to get married, you must have me.

riddle_original: انا لي تزاديت ف سطات و وليت وزير الداخلية مع الحسن الثاني
riddle_english: I was born in Settat and became Minister of the Interior under Hassan II.

riddle_original: أنا أعلى وثيقة فلبلاد، بيا كتنظم السلطات والحقوق والواجبات ديال المواطنين، والمغاربة صوتوا عليا بنعم فالاستفتاء ديال 2011
riddle_english: I am the highest document in the country, through me authorities, rights, and duties of citizens are organized, and Moroccans voted yes for me in the 2011 referendum.

riddle_original: أنا لي كايختارني الملك من الحزب لي ربح أكبر عدد ديال المقاعد ف لانتخابات، وأنا لي كنسير الشؤون اليومية ديال لبلاد.
riddle_english: I am the one chosen by the King from the party that won the most seats in the elections, and I am the one who manages the daily affairs of the country.

riddle_original: حنا هوما الأحزاب لي ما دخلناش للحكومة, خدمتنا هي نراقبو الخدمات ديال الوزارات و نعطيوهوم انتقادات على داكشي لي كا يديرو.
riddle_english: We are the parties that did not enter the government; our job is to monitor the services of the ministries and give them criticism on what they are doing.

riddle_original: أنا لي خرجو فيا المغاربة من كل مدينة، هازين غير الراية والقرآن، وبيا رجعنا الصحرا المغربية
riddle_english: I am the one for which Moroccans from every city came out, carrying only the flag and the Quran, and through me we reclaimed the Moroccan Sahara.

riddle_original: أنا مدينة قديمة بناوني الرومان، سواريا والفسيفساء ديالي باقين شاهدين على الزمان، وجيت حدا مكناس.
riddle_english: I am an ancient city built by the Romans; my columns and mosaics still bear witness to time, and I am located near Meknes.

riddle_original: أنا لي واقفة فالعاصمة، صومعتي مشهورة وما كاملاش فالبني، ودايرين بيا السواري.
riddle_english: I am the one standing in the capital, my minaret is famous and incomplete, and I am surrounded by columns.

riddle_original: انا لحرب لي وقعات معا فرانسا حيت لمغرب كان كايدعم لمقاومة د لجزائر
riddle_english: I am the war that took place with France because Morocco was supporting the Algerian resistance.

riddle_original: أنا أول دقة صحيحة كلاوها السبنيول ف جبال الريف، بيا بداو الانتصارات ديال عبد الكريم الخطابي
riddle_english: I am the first true blow the Spaniards received in the Rif Mountains, and with me began the victories of Abd el-Krim el-Khattabi.

riddle_original: انا لي تزاديت ف طنجة و صافرت ف شلا بلدان و 3 د لقارات. لكتاب ديالي معروف و مهم يلا بغتي تفهم لفترة لي عشت فيها و دول لي زرتها
riddle_english: I was born in Tangier and traveled to many countries and three continents. My book is famous and important if you want to understand the period I lived in and the countries I visited.

riddle_original: انا لي درت راسي ملك و حكمت شرق د لمغرب لمدة سبع سنين
riddle_english: I am the one who made myself king and ruled eastern Morocco for seven years.

riddle_original: تنفا أمير و بعد رجوعو ولا ملك
riddle_english: An prince was exiled and after his return he became a king

riddle_original: العام فاش ولا العام الأمازيغي معترف بيه كعطلة
riddle_english: In which year did the Amazigh New Year become recognized as a holiday?

riddle_original: اخر سلطان ديال المغرب
riddle_english: The last Sultan of Morocco

riddle_original: أنا لي عالي فالمغرب وكاع شمال إفريقيا،ديما مغطي بالثلج، والناس كتجي من كل بلاصة باش تسلقني
riddle_english: I am tall in Morocco and all of North Africa, always covered in snow, and people come from everywhere to climb me.

riddle_original: أنا لي مشهورة بالرملة، كيجيو ليا الناس باش يركبو الجمال، و باش يتدفنو فيا باش يتداواو من البرودة
riddle_english: I am famous for my sand, people come to me to ride camels, and to be buried in me to be treated for coldness.

riddle_original: انا لي نصي ف لبحر و نصي ف لارض. فين ما ضرتي وصتي تلقا مطلوقة لمزيكة.
riddle_english: I have half of me in the sea and half of me on land. Wherever you walk inside me you will find music playing.

riddle_original: أنا الجبال لي شادة شمال المغرب, كانطل على البحر الأبيض المتوسط, و ديما طبيعتي خضرا
riddle_english: I am the mountains that border northern Morocco, I look out over the Mediterranean Sea, and my nature is always green.

riddle_original: أنا مدينة فجنوب البلاد، مشهورة بالدلاح وواحات النخل، وعندي بلاكة معروفة مكتوب فيها 52 يوم
riddle_english: I am a city in the south of the country, famous for watermelon and palm oases, and I have a well-known sign that says 52 days.

riddle_original: انا لواد لي كايبدا مي جبال لاطلس و كايحبس حتال ازمور فين كيكب ف لمحيط لاطلسي
riddle_english: I am the river that starts from the Atlas Mountains and stops at Azemmour where it flows into the Atlantic Ocean.

riddle_original: مدينة معروفة بالتلج ديالها
riddle_english: A city known for its snow.

riddle_original: زعفراني هو أحسن زعفران فالمغرب
riddle_english: My saffron is the best saffron in Morocco.

riddle_original: كايعيطو عليها بسمية المدينة الزرقا
riddle_english: They call it by the name of the Blue City.

riddle_original: أطول واد فالبلاد، كيبدا فالأطلس العالي
riddle_english: The longest valley in the country, it starts in the High Atlas.

riddle_original: أنا لي عندي تلاتة ديال الوتار، وصوتي غليظ، وبيا المعلم كايدير الليلة الكناوية
riddle_english: I have three strings, my voice is deep, and with me the master performs the Gnawa night.

riddle_original: أنا لي موسيقتي كتلعب بالكمبري والقراقب، ومهرجاني الكبير كايتجامعو فيه الناس كولا عام فالصويرة
riddle_english: I have my music played with the guembri and krakebs, and my big festival brings people together every year in Essaouira.

riddle_original: أنا رقصة تقليدية معروفة فزاكورة ودرعة، كيشطحوها الرجال والعيالات مجموعين، وسميتي جات من واحد البلاصة فرجليك
riddle_english: I am a traditional dance known in Zagora and Draa, danced by men and women together, and my name comes from a part of your feet.

riddle_original: انا لفن لي كيزوقو بيه لخشب و يديروه ف ديور اولا لحيوط ديالهم
riddle_english: I am the art used to decorate wood and put in houses or on their walls.

riddle_original: انا اشهر رسامة مغربية. تزاديت ف شتوكة و ولدي حتا هوا رسام كبير.
riddle_english: I am the most famous Moroccan female painter. I was born in Chtouka, and my son is also a great painter.

riddle_original: انا لموسيقى لي كيطلقوها ف اي عرس ولا اي حاجة فيها شطيح و نشاط
riddle_english: I am the music they play at any wedding or any event with dancing and joy.

riddle_original: انا لي كيشطحو بيا لعيالات ف لمناسبات و يغنيو. مصنوعة كلي غي من طين و جلد
riddle_english: I am what women dance with at celebrations while singing. I am made entirely of clay and skin.

riddle_original: انا لي كيشطحو فوقي ف لعرس. كنكون ف لوصت و كيشحو فوقي رجال و عيالات
riddle_english: I am the one people dance on at a wedding. I am in the middle and men and women dance on me.

riddle_original: أنا رقصة أمازيغية قديمة معروفة فالأطلس، كيتجمعوا فيا الرجال والعيالات على شكل دائرة ولا صف، وكنشطحو على البندير
riddle_english: I am an ancient Amazigh dance known in the Atlas, where men and women gather in a circle or a row, and we dance to the bendir.

riddle_original: انا رواية لي كتبها مغربي ب فرونسي. قراوها ناس ب لخاطر ولا بزز باش يوجدو لجهوي
riddle_english: I am a novel written by a Moroccan in French. People read it willingly or were forced to in order to prepare for the regional exam.

riddle_original: انا رياضة لي لاغلبية كتكون ف لموسم. كلا سربة كتركب علا لعودان ديالها و لي متناسقين مزيان هما لي كيربحو
riddle_english: I am a sport that mostly takes place during the festival season. Each troop rides its horses, and those who are well-coordinated are the ones who win.

riddle_original: أنا بطل مغربي فالجرا، الروكور ديالي ف 1500 متر حتى واحد ما يوصلو
riddle_english: I am a Moroccan running hero, my record in the 1500 meters is one that no one can reach.

riddle_original: أنا سباق طويل وصعيب، كنجريو فيا أيام وسط الرملة والشمس ديال الصحراء، وكل واحد هاز زادو على ظهرو
riddle_english: I am a long and difficult race, where we run for days in the middle of the sand and the sun of the desert, and everyone carries their provisions on their back.

riddle_original: أنا ماتش كنقسم كازا على جوج، نص خضر ونص حمر، ونهار كا نتلعب القهاوي كيعمرو والتيفوات كايتهزو فالسما.
riddle_english: I am a match that divides Casablanca into two, half green and half red, and on the day I am played, cafes fill up and tifos are raised in the sky.

riddle_original: انا فرقة د لكورة لي عندها اكثر عدد ديال لبطولات ف لمغرب
riddle_english: I am the football team that has the most championships in Morocco.

riddle_original: انا لفريق د لكورة لي بداه لحسن ثاني من لعسكر
riddle_english: I am the football team that was founded by Hassan II from the military.

riddle_original: انا اول فريق عربي وصل لفينال ديال كاس لعالم للاندية
riddle_english: I was the first Arab team to reach the final of the FIFA Club World Cup.

riddle_original: انا اللاعب لي معروف ب سيزووات. نقدر نمارركي سيزو و مانماركيش كرة ساهلة
riddle_english: I am the player known for bicycle kicks. I can score a bicycle kick and not score an easy ball.

riddle_original: انا لي لعبت الذهاب ديال ديربي معا الرجاء و الاياب معا الوداد ف نفس لعام
riddle_english: I am the one who played the first leg of the derby with Raja and the second leg with Wydad in the same year.

riddle_original: أنا لي حطمت أرقام قياسية فالمسافات المتوسطة و الطويلة فالثمانينات, رفعت الراية ديال المغرب فلوس انجلوس
riddle_english: I am the one who broke world records in middle and long distances in the eighties, and I raised the Moroccan flag in Los Angeles.

riddle_original: أنا لي ملون ومرسوم بهندسة زوينة، فالحيوط وفالارض د الحمام والرياض كتلقاني، وبيا كيتعرف الصانع المغربي
riddle_english: I am colored and drawn with beautiful geometry, you find me on the walls and floors of bathrooms and riads, and through me, the Moroccan craftsman is known.

riddle_original: انا لي كايخدمو بيا باش يدڭو شي حاجة و يرجعوها غبرة
riddle_english: I am the one they use to crush something and turn it into dust.

riddle_original: الحيوان لي عندو أكبر قيمة عند مغربي
riddle_english: The animal that has the most value for a Moroccan.

riddle_original: انا لي ف ايا دار تلقاني يصاوبو بيا اتاي. شكل ديالي مصاوب باش نخوي اتاي نيشان ف لكاس.
riddle_english: I am in every house, used to make tea. My shape is designed to pour tea straight into the glass.

riddle_original: انا لي كايشعلو بيا لعافية باش يشويو ولا يصاوبو اتاي. حتا الا بغيتي تبرد نسوط عليك
riddle_english: I am the one they light fire with to grill or make tea. Even if you want to cool down, I can blow on you.

riddle_original: أنا شجرة فينما مشيتي فسوس تلقاني، زيت دياالي ما خلا بلاصة فالعالم، وبيا كا تفتخر لبلاد و انا ما كاين فتا بلاد أخرى
riddle_english: I am a tree; wherever you go in the Souss region, you will find me. My oil has reached every place in the world, and the country is proud of me, yet I do not exist in any other country.

riddle_original: أنا لي فالسقف كينقشني المعلم، بيض وفيا الزواق، وبيا كتفخر كل دار
riddle_english: I am on the ceiling, carved by the master; I am white with decorations, and every house is proud of me.

riddle_original: انا لي كل دار كاتقاد لخبز ديالها و كاتجيبو يطيب فيا. حتا لي ماصاوبش لخبز يقدر يشريه مني
riddle_english: I am the one for whom every house prepares its dough and brings it to be baked in me. Even those who didn't make dough can buy it from me.

riddle_original: انا مصاوب من طين و كيصوبو فيا اكلة مغربية مشهورة
riddle_english: I am made of clay and a famous Moroccan dish is prepared in me.

riddle_original: انا لي كتلقاني ف كلا صالون مفرشة
riddle_english: I am the one you find in every salon, spread out.

riddle_original: أنا لي مصنوع من الخشب وعندي مسمار ف راسي، كدور عليا الخيط باش نشطح وندور
riddle_english: I am made of wood and have a nail in my head; I wrap a string around myself to dance and spin.

riddle_original: أنا لي لوني وردي ومذاقي د الرمان، عزيز على الكبير والصغير، وديما مصاحب مع الميلفوي
riddle_english: I am pink in color and have the taste of pomegranate, dear to the old and the young, and always accompanied by the mille-feuille.

riddle_original: أنا لي فيا لي مغمض عينيه كيحسب بالجهد، والخرين هربانين كايقلبو فين يتخباو
riddle_english: I am the one where someone has their eyes closed and is counting loudly, while the others have run away and are looking for a place to hide.

riddle_original: انا لي فيا وحدين كايهربو و وحدين كايتبعوم و لي تشد خاص يتبع حتا هوا
riddle_english: I am the one where some are running away and some are following them, and whoever is caught must also start following.

riddle_original: انا نهار لوحيد لي تقدر ترش فيه لما علا بنادم حتا لي مكتعرفوش مزيان
riddle_english: I am the only day where you can splash water on people, even those you do not know well.

riddle_original: انا نهار لي فيه دراري صغار كيخرجو يغنيو و يشطحو و ناس كايعطيوهم فاكية و فلوس
riddle_english: I am a day when young children go out singing and dancing, and people give them dried fruits and money.

riddle_original: جوج تالمرات فالعام، كينتاضروها الصغار، وكايتهربو منها لكبار لي ماشي سخيين
riddle_english: Twice a year, children wait for it, and the adults who are not generous run away from it.

riddle_original: انا لي فيا الف ورقة و كنكون ديما ساوية درهم. كتلقاني ف اي حانوت ولا محلبة
riddle_english: I have a thousand leaves and I am always worth a dirham. You can find me in any shop or dairy.

riddle_original: انا لي كيلعبوني ب كرات صغيرة كتبري
riddle_english: I am the one who is played with small, shiny balls.

riddle_original: لعبة مسميا على عدد، وأغلبيتها كدوزو علا رجل وحدة
riddle_english: A game named after a number, and most of it is played on one leg.

riddle_original: انا لي كايجيو ليا ناس مرا ف سيمانة. فيا لبارد و سخون علا حساب جهد ديالك
riddle_english: I am the one people come to see once a week. I have both cold and hot, depending on your effort.

riddle_original: انا لحفلة لي كايديرو ناس ف نهار سابع ملي كيتزاد شي واحد
riddle_english: I am the party that people throw on the seventh day after someone is born.

riddle_original: انا نهار لي كيكون قبل من لعرس وكيتجمعو فيه لعائلة و صحابات لعروسة باش يحتافلو بيها
riddle_english: I am the day that comes before the wedding, when the family and the bride's friends gather to celebrate her.

riddle_original: أنا لي ديما مزاحمة بالناس، تلقى فيا الخضرة والنعناع و لي بغيتي بثمن قليل
riddle_english: I am always crowded with people, you find vegetables and mint in me, and whatever you want at a low price.

riddle_original: أنا لي ديما فالدرب، عندي تلقا كلشي من الخبز حتى للبوطة، واللي ماعندو فلوس كانقيد ليه فالكارني
riddle_english: I am always in the neighborhood, you can find everything with me from bread to gas cylinders, and for those who have no money, I write it down for them in the notebook.

riddle_original: أنا سوق، فيا الحوايج ديال البال و داكشي القديم، ولي بغا يتقدى بالرخا ويلقى الهمزة كيقصدني
riddle_english: I am a market, I have second-hand clothes and old things, and whoever wants to shop cheaply and find a bargain comes to me.

riddle_original: انا لي كتلبس و تدير لماكياج لعروسات نهار لعرس
riddle_english: I am the one who dresses and applies makeup to brides on their wedding day.

riddle_original: انا لي كيحكليك ف لحمام بلاصت ماتحك ضهرك علا لحيط
riddle_english: I am the one who rubs for you in the hammam instead of you rubbing your back against the wall.

riddle_original: انا طاكسي لي كتشدو فاش كتبغي تسافر من مدينة ل مدينة
riddle_english: I am a taxi that you take when you want to travel from city to city

riddle_original: ف كلا دار كتلقاني كينشرو فيا لحوايج و كيكون فيا لبارابول
riddle_english: You find me in every house, clothes are hung on me, and the satellite dish is placed on me.

riddle_original: انا لي تقدر تصاوب بيا طاجين ولا تاكلني غي ب لخبز. كنكون ف ڭاع لالوان و لمهم الا كليتيني متنساش تحيد لعضم
riddle_english: I am the one you can use to make a tagine or eat with just bread. I come in all colors, and importantly, if you eat me, don't forget to remove the pit.

riddle_original: صغيرة, كتزاد فأتاي. فاش كتكبر و كتغطيها قشرة دهبية, تقد تشربها بوحدها.
riddle_english: Small, it is added to tea. When it grows and is covered by a golden skin, you can drink it on its own.

riddle_original: انا ماكلة لي باش تصاوبني خاص تصاوب مسمن هوا لول. لاغلبية كنكون مصاوبة ب دجاج
riddle_english: I am a dish that requires making msemmen first in order to prepare me. Most of the time, I am made with chicken.

riddle_original: أنا لي عامرة بالقطاني والربيع، ريحتي عاطية فالدرب، و صحابي ديما هما التمر والمغرفة
riddle_english: I am full of legumes and herbs, my scent fills the neighborhood, and my companions are always dates and the ladle.

riddle_original: أنا لي كنجمع بين الحلو والمالح، ورقتي مقرمشة ومزوقة بالقرفة والسكر كلاصي، و كانجي معمرة بالدجاج واللوز ولا الحوت، وكانكون فالعراسات والمناسبات
riddle_english: I am the one who combines sweet and savory, my pastry is crispy and decorated with cinnamon and powdered sugar, and I come filled with chicken and almonds or fish, and I am served at weddings and special occasions.

riddle_original: أنا لي مطوية ومشبكة، ومغمسة فالعسل ومزوقة بالزنجلان
riddle_english: I am folded and latticed, dipped in honey and decorated with sesame seeds.

riddle_original: أنا أول ما كتاكل فالعيد الكبير
riddle_english: I am the first thing you eat on Eid al-Adha.

riddle_original: أنا أكلة مراكشية، كنطيب ف قلوشة ديال الطين عند الفرناتشي
riddle_english: I am a Marrakesh dish, cooked in a clay jar at the fernatchi.

riddle_original: حاضرة معا اتاي فكل عيد و داغا كنتفرتت
riddle_english: I am present with tea at every feast, and I crumble quickly.

riddle_original: انا هوا لبانكيك د لمغرب. كتلقا ديما حدايا اتاي و كانجي مزيان معا لعسل
riddle_english: I am the pancake of Morocco. You always find tea next to me and I go well with honey.

riddle_original: كيلبسوني ناس معا لفوقية ولا جلابة ف رجليهم
riddle_english: People wear me with a fouqia or a djellaba on their feet.

riddle_original: أنا لي لباس مغربي أصيل، كيلبسوني الرجال والعيالات، والسر ديالي كلو فداك القب لي لاصق فيا

riddle_original: Гэтая народная назва зоркі, апетай класікам, добра вядомая беларускім жанчынам.
riddle_english: This folk name of a star, which was sung by a classic, is well known to Belarusian women.

riddle_original: Раней гэта быў сеткавы магазін з грашыма ў назве, а цяпер яго месца заняў "святы" з Брэста.
riddle_english: It used to be a chain store with money in the name, but now its place has been taken by a "saint" from Brest.

riddle_original: Купюра з яе выявай аформлена пад колер чырвонай (а зусім не белай) цэглы, з якой яна і пабудавана.
riddle_english: The banknote with its image is decorated in the color of the red (and not white) brick from which it is built.

riddle_original: Каб набыць газету на транспартным прыпынку, шукайце гэтае слова на шыльдзе.
riddle_english: To buy a newspaper at a transport stop, look for this word on the signboard.
riddle_note: Belsayuzdruk is more common, Beldruk is a 2019 rebranding

riddle_original: Пад гэтым брэндам з 1990-х гадоў выпускае сваю прадукцыю колішні бровар дарэвалюцыйнага арыстакрата.
riddle_english: Since the 1990s, the former brewery of a pre-revolutionary aristocrat has been producing its products under this brand.

riddle_original: Літара на ружовым пластыкавым кругляшы.
riddle_english: The letter on a round pink plastic token.
riddle_note: the question refers to Minsk subway tokens

riddle_original: Варта мець яго з сабой, каб не плаціць штраф, ходзячы ўздоўж дарог позна ўвечары.
riddle_english: It is worth having it with you to avoid paying a fine when walking along the roads late at night.

riddle_original: Цяпер назва гэтага аператара складаецца з літары і лічбы, а як ён называўся раней?
riddle_english: Now the name of this operator consists of a letter and a number, but what was it called before?

riddle_original: Калі вам раптам стане блага, трэба ўзгадаць гэты просты лік.
riddle_english: If you suddenly feel unwell, you need to recall this prime number.

riddle_original: Ён калісьці быў на грошах, яму абавязаны сваёй назвай трава і настойка, а яго дзіцяня асацыюецца з месцам летняга адпачынку.
riddle_english: It was once depicted on money, it lends its name to grass and tincture, and its offspring is associated with a summer vacation spot.
author_credit: Vladislav Poritski, Oksana Volchek, Ilia Afanasev

riddle_original: Адзін з іх нагадваў паэту XX стагоддзя пра спадчыну, а двух можна пабачыць на пляшцы моцнага напою.
riddle_english: One of them reminded the 20th-century poet of his heritage, and two can be seen on a bottle of strong drink.

riddle_original: Ён у творах паэта, які памёр маладым, выступае і як імпартазамяшчальнік, і як напамін, што сярод карыснага ёсць месца для прыгожага.
riddle_english: In the works of the poet who died young, it is both an import substitute and a reminder that there is a place for the beautiful among the useful.

riddle_original: Нягледзячы на тое, што гэтая птушка вельмі разумная, у беларускай прыказцы з ёй параўноўваюць праставатага вяскоўца.
riddle_english: Although this bird is very intelligent, a simple-minded villager is compared to it in a Belarusian proverb.
author_credit: Ilia Afanasev, Vladislav Poritski, Oksana Volchek

riddle_original: Кара гэтага дрэва, па адной з версій, дала назву гораду, у якога ёсць французскі цёзка.
riddle_english: The bark of this tree, according to one version, gave the name to the city that has a French namesake.

riddle_original: Не толькі жывёла, але і перыядычнае выданне для аматараў пасмяяцца, і псеўданім рэп-выканаўцы.
riddle_english: Not only an animal but also a periodical for those who like to laugh and a rap artist's pseudonym.
author_credit: Vladislav Poritski, Oksana Volchek, Ilia Afanasev

riddle_original: Пах гэтай расліны нагадвае герою верша пра згубленае юнацкае каханне.
riddle_english: The smell of this plant reminds the poem's hero about his youthful love.

riddle_original: У гэтую птушку, згодна з беларускім паданнем, ператварылася жанчына, якая не клапацілася пра сваіх дзяцей.
riddle_english: According to Belarusian legend, a woman who did not take care of her children turned into this bird.

riddle_original: Названая ў гонар птушкі ягада, збіраць якую можа быць рызыкоўна.
riddle_english: This berry, named after a bird, can be risky to pick.

riddle_original: Да гэтай лятучай істоты звяртаецца з папрокам хлопец у хрэстаматыйным вершы.
riddle_english: A boy in a textbook poem addresses this flying creature with reproach.

riddle_original: Менавіта так называўся хот-дог, які можна было набыць пад шыльдай з двума словамі і арнаментам.
riddle_english: The name of the hot dog that once could be purchased under a sign with two words and an ornament.

riddle_original: Якая жывёла нагадвае аматарам салодкага пра сталіцу найстаражытнейшага беларускага княства?
riddle_english: What animal reminds sweet tooth lovers of the capital of the oldest Belarusian principality?

riddle_original: Пра яе смак спрачаюцца прыхільнікі двух гарадоў: на поўначы і на паўднёвым усходзе Беларусі.
riddle_english: Fans of two cities, in the north and southeast of Belarus, argue about its taste.

riddle_original: Імя цмока на абгортцы хрумсткіх ласункаў з абласнога цэнтра.
riddle_english: The name of the dragon on the wrapper of crispy treats from the regional center.

riddle_original: Пасля гэтай ежы ў рыфмаваным выслоўі пра дастойны ўзровень жыцця часам яшчэ згадваюць аўтамабіль.
riddle_english: After this food, a car is sometimes mentioned in a rhymed saying about a decent standard of living.

riddle_original: Гэты горад славіцца сваім бела-ружовым смакоццем.
riddle_english: This city is famous for its white and pink yummies.

riddle_original: Гэтай айчыннай альтэрнатывай піцы славіцца райцэнтр на Магілёўшчыне.
riddle_english: A district center in the Mogilev region is famous for this domestic alternative to pizza.

riddle_original: Легендарны аўтар гэтай мясной стравы з соусам насіў тое ж прозвішча, што і каханая паэта.
riddle_english: The legendary author of this meat dish with sauce had the same surname as the poet's beloved girl.

riddle_original: Імя гэтага бунтара носіць вытворца палескіх ласункаў у рознакаляровых абгортках.
riddle_english: The name of this rebel is borne by the manufacturer of Polesie treats in multi-colored wrappers.

riddle_original: Аснова беларускай кухні, ад назвы якой нават утвораны жартаўлівы этнонім.
riddle_english: The basis of Belarusian cuisine, the name of which even gave rise to a humorous ethnonym.

riddle_original: ফরজের নামে উঠল ঢেউ, ঘর ছাড়িয়ে ক্ষেতে, নামাজের সুর মিশে গেল অধিকার চাওয়ার রেতে।
riddle_english: Waves rose in the name of duty, leaving the house and entering the fields, the melody of prayer mingled with the cry of demanding rights.
human_answer_comment:
Md Rabius Sany Apu All the riddles are grammatically correct, and the “Reference Answers (Original)” are valid. Although I couldn’t solve all of them, someone in Bangladesh would likely be able to figure them out with a little hint. The riddles are a mix of collected and newly created ones. The collected riddles felt more difficult due to  less familiar synonyms.
P.S. Some of my wrong answers could be an alternative possible answer, such as Number 32, 41, 80, 93, 94.

riddle_original:
মাথায় কাপড়, কথায় আগুন, জমিদারি টলে,
নামটি উঠলেই বাঁশের শব্দ ইতিহাস জুড়ে দোলে।
riddle_english: Cloth on the head, fire in the mouth, zamindari toll, the sound of bamboo echoes throughout history as soon as the name is mentioned.

riddle_original:
আলো ছিল নামে, হাতে ছিল রাত,
মাস্টার হয়েও কাঁপিয়ে দিল লোহার পাহারাদার ঘাট।
riddle_english: Light was in his name, night was in his hand, Even though he was a master, the iron guard of the wharf trembled.

riddle_original:
কাগমারী সম্মেলনে বিদায়ের সুর,
"আসসালামু আলাইকুম" ধ্বনি বহুদূর।
পাক-মার্কিন চুক্তি মানি নাই ভাই,
লাল মওলানা ছাড়া কারে আর পাই?
riddle_english:
The farewell tune at the Kagmari conference,
"Assalamu Alaikum" sounds far away.
I don't accept the Pakistan-US agreement, brother,
Who else can I get except Lal Maulana?

riddle_original:
আটটি ফাল্গুন, একুশের রাত,
বাংলাকে কেড়ে নিতে চেয়েছিল ঘাত।
জিন্নাহর দম্ভ চূর্ণ যে মাঠে,
রক্তের অক্ষরে ইতিহাস কাটে।
riddle_english:
On the 8th of Falgun, the night of the 21st,
Enemy wanted to take away Bengal.
On the field where Jinnah's pride was crushed,
History is written in letters of blood.

riddle_original:
ক্যালেন্ডারের পাতা আমি, অথচ স্বৈরাচারের শেষ,
চব্বিশের ছাত্র-জনতা বদলে দিল এই দেশ।
riddle_english: I am a page on the calendar, yet the end of dictatorship, the students of the 24 years old changed this country.

riddle_original:
আমি কোনো 'পোস্টার' নই, তবু বুকে লেখা স্লোগান,
নব্বইয়ের রাজপথে স্বৈরাচার তাড়াতে দিলাম প্রাণ।
riddle_english: I am not a 'poster', yet the slogan written on my chest is, "I gave my life to drive out tyranny on the streets of the 1990s."

riddle_original:
ভারতের এক শহর আমি, অথচ মামলা হলো বাংলায়,
৩৫ জন বন্দি হলাম পাকিস্তানের চতুর এক লালসায়।
riddle_english: I am from a city in India, but the case was filed in Bengal, 35 people were arrested in a clever attempt by Pakistan.

riddle_original:
নামেতে আমার আদেশ, কিন্তু নব্বইয়ে খাটেনি কোনো জোর,
নয় বছরের গদি ছেড়ে জেনারেল দেখলেন পরাজয়ের ঘোর
riddle_english: My orders were in the name, but no force was used at nineties, the general left the throne of nine years and saw the horror of defeat
reference_answer_english: The fall of Hussain Muhammad Ershad
human_answer_comment: r.sany.apu@gmail.com I used "জানিনা" or "No clue" when I coundn't guess any possible answer. This can be consided as 0: Completely Wrong. Suggestion: A new class -1: No Clue, could be added to the Rating of Human Answer.

riddle_original:
আমি কোনো 'দলিল' নই, তবু কোটি মানুষের মুক্তির কাব্যের গান,
আমার একটি মাত্র 'আঙুল' কাঁপিয়ে দিল মিলিটারির সব প্ল্যান।
মাত্র আঠারো মিনিটে আমি পাল্টে দিলাম  মার্চের সেই বেলা,
আমি কোন্ ভাষণ, যা নিয়ে আজও চলে রাজনীতির খেলা?
riddle_english:
I am not any 'deed', yet I am a poetic song of liberation for millions of people,
My single 'finger' shook all the military's plans.
In just eighteen minutes, I changed that day in March,
What kind of speech am I, about which the game of politics is still played today?
human_answer_original: বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমানের ঐতিহাসিক ভাষণ

riddle_original: নামেতে সোনা, মাটিতে ধুল, রাজধানী ছিলাম, আজ স্মৃতির ফুল।
riddle_english: Gold in name, dust on the ground, I was the capital, today it is a flower of memory.

riddle_original:
গম্বুজ গুনে শেষ না হয়, ইটে লেখা দাগ,
নাম লুকানো সংখ্যার ভেতর, তবু দেয়াল জাগ।
riddle_english: The domes are endless, the marks written on the bricks, the names hidden within the numbers, yet the walls remain awake.

riddle_original: অতীশ গেল দূর দেশে, তিব্বতে যার ধ্বনি, শুরুটা এই মাটিতেই, কোন সেই জন্মভূমি?
riddle_english: Atish has gone to a distant land, whose sound is in Tibet, but whose beginning is in this land, what is that homeland?

riddle_original: সমুদ্র ছুঁয়ে নাম পেয়েছি, পূর্ব বাংলার শেষ ধরেছি। প্রাচীন গ্রন্থে নাম লেখা রয়, কোন জনপদের পরিচয়?
riddle_english: I got my name by touching the sea, I have reached the end of East Bengal. The name is written in ancient books, what is the identity of the territory?

riddle_original:
বন্দর ছিলাম, নদী ছিল সাথি,
রোমান মুদ্রা পেয়েছি খাঁটি।
মাটির তলে বাণিজ্যের দাগ,
কোন নগরের প্রাচীন আগ?
riddle_english:
I was a port, the river was my companion,
I received authentic Roman coins.
The traces of trade under the ground,
The ancient ruins of which city?

riddle_original: তিন অক্ষরে নাম আমার, নদীর পাড়ে মাঠ। শেষের অক্ষর বাদ দিলে, ভয়েতে পালাই তাত।
riddle_english: My name is in three letters, a field on the bank of the river. If I omit the last letter, I will run away in fear.

riddle_original:
নদীতেই জন্ম, নদীতেই শেষ,
দিল্লিকে ভুলে আমি স্বাধীন এক দেশ।
বাহাদুর তখতের পতন যেথা ভাই,
ইতিহাসে সেই প্রথম স্বাধীনতা পাই।
riddle_english:
Born in the river, ended in the river,
Forgetting Delhi, I am an independent country.
Brother, where the Bahadur Takht fell,
We got the first freedom in history.
reference_answer_original: ফখরুদ্দিন মোবারক শাহ (সোনারগাঁওয়ে স্বাধীন সুলতানি আমল)
reference_answer_english: Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah (Independent Sultanate period in Sonargaon)

riddle_original:
লিপিতেই বেঁচে আছি, পাথরের গায়,
সেন বংশের শেষ তরী যেথা ডোবে হায়।
লক্ষ্মণ পালালো কোন্ খিলজির ডরে,
ইতিহাস লেখা আছে নদীটির চরে?
riddle_english:
I live in the script, in the body of stone,
Where the last ship of the Sena dynasty will sink, alas.
Which Khilji did Lakshman flee in fear,
Is history written on the banks of the river?

riddle_original:
রঙ ছিল আগে, পরে হলো ক্ষত, নামেই তার ফাঁদ,
ক্ষেতের বুকেই উঠল শেষে প্রতিবাদের স্বরবাদ।
riddle_english: First there was color, then there was a wound, its name was its trap, and finally, the voice of protest rose in the field.

riddle_original:
আমের বাগানে সেই রক্তের দাগ,
নবাবের হারে বাড়ে ফিরিঙ্গির ভাগ।
মীরজাফর নাম নয়, বিশ্বাসঘাতকতার ছায়া,
কোন্ সে নদীর তীরে মরে গেল মায়া?
riddle_english:
Blood stains the soil where mango trees grow,
The Nawab’s defeat made the foreign share grow.
Mir Jafar is no longer a name, but betrayal's cold art,
On the banks of which river died Bengal's true heart?

riddle_original: পাঁচ অক্ষরে নাম তার, একটি জেলা আছে। শেষের তিন অক্ষর বাদ দিলে রঙের নাম হবে।
riddle_english: It has a five-letter name, and a district. If you remove the last three letters, it becomes the name of a color.

riddle_original: কোথায় নদী আছে কিন্তুু পানি  নেই পাহাড় আছে কিন্তু পাথর নেই দেশ আছে কিন্তু লোক নেই?
riddle_english: Where is there a river but no water, a mountain but no stones, a country but no people?

riddle_original: আমি দুই দেশে আছি, বাঘ আমার বাসিন্দা, লবণ জলে আমার শিকড়। আমি কী?
riddle_english: I am in two countries, the tiger is my resident, my roots are in salt water. What am I?

riddle_original: পাহাড় বুকে জন্ম তার, সমতলে তার ঢল, নাম বদলাতে বদলাতে নামে সাগর-তল।
riddle_english: It was born on the mountainside, it flourished on the plains, and its name changed and changed, and it was called the ocean floor.

riddle_original: প্রবাল দিয়ে গড়া দ্বীপ, নীল সাগরের টিপ, টেকনাফ ছেড়ে যেতে হয় চড়ে বড় শিপ।
riddle_english: An island made of coral, bindi of the blue sea, To leave Teknaf you have to board a large ship.

riddle_original: পাহাড় ঘেরা বিশাল হ্রদ, বাঁধের জলে গড়া, রাঙামাটির বুকে যেন নীল গালিচা পড়া।
riddle_english: A huge lake surrounded by mountains, formed by dam water, spreads like a blue carpet across Rangamati.

riddle_original: সূর্য ওঠা, সূর্য ডোবা, একই সৈকতে হয়, সাগরকন্যা নামে তার ভূগোলে পরিচয়।
riddle_english: The sun rises and sets on the same beach, and is known in geography as the daughter of the sea.

riddle_original: পানি এলে সাগর যেন, পানি গেলে মাঠ, ধানও ধরে, নাওও চলে, এমন কিসের ঘাট?
riddle_english: When the water comes, it's like an ocean, when the water goes, it's like a field, rice can be grown, and boat can also be driven, what kind of wharf is this?

riddle_original: লাল মাটির উঁচুনিচু, রুক্ষ তারই ভূমি, উত্তরের এই প্রাচীন দেশে ইতিহাসের ঘুমি।
riddle_english: The red soil is uneven and rugged; in this ancient land of the north, history lies asleep.

riddle_original: নদীর বুকে জাগে আবার, আবার যায় ভেসে, মানুষ গিয়ে ঘর তোলে তবু টেকে না সে বেশে।
riddle_english: It wakes up again on the riverbank, drifts away again, people go and build houses, but it still doesn't survive.

riddle_original:
দেহে কষ্ট, মনে গান,
চৈত্র শেষে জাগে প্রাণ।
আগুন, কাঁটা, ভক্তির ঢেউ,
কোন উৎসব বলো এই ঢেউ?
riddle_english:
Pain in the body, song in the mind,
The soul awakens at the end of Chaitra.
Fire, thorns, waves of devotion,
What festival is this wave?

riddle_original: বছরের শেষে নয়, শস্যের পরে, হাঁড়ি ভরে সুখ নামে ঘরে। পিঠা, ধান আর নতুন চাল, কোন আনন্দে খুলে যায় তাল?
riddle_english: Not at the end of the year, but after the harvest, the pots of happiness bestows upon houses. Cakes, rice and new rice, with what joy do the palms open?

riddle_original:
আমি কোনো 'আয়না' নই, তবু রক্ত মাখা রূপ দেখাই,
নীল চাষীর চোখের জল মোর পাতায় পাতায় পাই।
riddle_english: I am not a 'mirror', yet I show my blood-stained form, I find the tears of the indigo farmer on my pages.

riddle_original:
প্রশ্ন ছুঁড়ে, জবাব আসে,
কথার লড়াই সুরের পাশে।
মুখে মুখে ওঠে আগুন,
কোন সেই লোককবির ধুন?
riddle_english:
Questions are thrown, answers come,
The battle of words is next to the melody.
The fire rises in the mouth,
Which folk poet tune is that?

riddle_original:
মঞ্চে কাঁদি, মঞ্চে হাসি, রাতভর করি পালা,
গান, সংলাপ, রঙ মেখে বলো কোন সে গ্রামীণ জ্বালা?
riddle_english: I cry on stage, I laugh on stage, I dance all night long, Tell me, what is that rural passion, mixing songs, dialogues, and colors?

riddle_original:
দাঁড় টানিলে আমিও টানি, কণ্ঠে উঠে ঢেউ,
নদীর বুকে কাজের ছন্দে বলো আমি কে হে?
riddle_english: When you pull the rope, I pull too, waves rise in your voice, Tell me in the rhythm of work in the river's chest, who am I?

riddle_original:
কারবালার প্রান্তরে শোক, মৃত্যুর হাহাকার,
হাসান-হোসেনের আত্মত্যাগ, রক্তের পারাপার।
মীর মশাররফ হোসেন লিখেছেন মহাকাব্যিক ঢঙে,
কোন সে গদ্যকাহিনি, যা পড়া হয় গভীর রঙ্গে?
riddle_english: The mourning in the desert of Karbala, the wailing of death, the sacrifice of Hasan and Hossain, the crossing of blood. Mir Mosharraf Hossain wrote in an epic style, Which prose story is read in deep colors?

riddle_original:
যুদ্ধের দিন, রুমী গেল, ফেরে না আর ঘরে,
জাহানারা ইমামের কোন ডায়েরি আজো কাঁদায় পড়ে?
riddle_english: On the day of the war, Rumi left, never to return home, Which diary of Jahanara Imam still makes me cry?

riddle_original:
বই না হয়েও মুখে বাঁচি, কণ্ঠে কণ্ঠে যাই,
শোনার ভেতর পড়া মেলে, রাতের আসর পাই।
riddle_english:
Though not a book, I live on lips, from voice to voice I fly;
Within the act of listening, reading appears, and I find a place in night-time gatherings.
human_answer_comment:
r.sany.apu@gmail.com Though not a book, I live on lips; from voice to voice, I fly. Within the act of listening, reading appears, and I find a place in nighttime gatherings. My answer is: Nursery Rhymes.
In Bangladesh, especially in villages, children and mothers create rhythmic songs, particularly for nighttime, called “ছড়া গান (Chora Gaan).” These songs often remain unwritten and are passed down through generations. In my opinion, this could also be considered an alternative answer.

riddle_original:
ঠান্ডা নামে ডাকে সবাই, শীতের বস্তু নই,
পাতার গায়ে ঘর সাজিয়ে চুপচাপ বিছিয়ে রই।
riddle_english: Everyone calls it cold, I am not a winter thing, I make a house on the leaves and lie quietly.

riddle_original: গোল আছে, মাঠ আছে, পা দিয়ে সবাই মারে। হাত লাগালে ফাউল হয়, বল তো কী নাম তার রে?
riddle_english: There is a goal, there is a field, everyone kicks with their feet. Touching with hands is a foul, tell me what is its name?

riddle_original: কাঠের তৈরি শরীর আমার, বলকে করি তাড়া। ছক্কা-চার হাঁকিয়ে আমি, মাঠে তুলি সাড়া।
riddle_english: My body is made of wood, I chase the ball. Hitting sixes and fours, I create a stir on the field.

riddle_original: পাখির মতো পালক আছে, কিন্তু আমি পাখি নই। র‍্যাকেটের ঘা খেয়ে আমি, এদিক-ওদিক ছুটে যাই।
riddle_english: I have feathers like a bird, but I am not a bird. Struck by a racket, I dart here and there.

riddle_original: রাজা আছে, রানি আছে, নেইকো কোনো দেশ। সাদা-কালো ঘরগুলোতেই, এদের লড়াই শেষ।
riddle_english: There is a king, there is a queen, but no country. Their battle ends within black and white squares.

riddle_original: তিন ভাই দাঁড়িয়ে থাকি, মাথায় থাকে টুপি। বল লাগলেই পড়ে যাই, নিচু করে মুণ্ডি।
riddle_english: Three brothers stand together, wearing caps on their heads. The moment the ball hits, we fall down, lowering our heads.

riddle_original: ছোট্ট আমার শরীরখানি, গলার আওয়াজ ভারী। মাঠে আমি বাজলে পরে, সবাই থামতে বাধ্য রে ভাই।
riddle_english: Small is my body, but my voice is heavy/loud. When I sound off on the pitch, everyone is forced to stop, brother.

riddle_original: দুই হাতেতে পরিয়ে দেয়, ফোলা ফোলা গাল। রিংয়ের মাঝে লড়াই চলে, মারে কত তাল।
riddle_english: Worn on both hands, with puffy cheeks. The fight goes on in the ring, landing heavy blows.

riddle_original: হলুদ রঙের শরীর আমার, লোমে ঢাকা গায়। কোর্টের মাঝে এপাশ-ওপাশ, র‍্যাকেট আমায় ছুড়ে মারে তায়।
riddle_english: Yellow is my body, covered in fuzz. Across the court, side to side, the racket smashes me away.

riddle_original: জল আছে কিন্তু পুকুর নয়, হাত-পা ছুড়ে সবাই যায়। এপার থেকে ওপার গিয়ে, মেডেল গলায় ঝুলিয়ে নেয়।
riddle_english: There is water but it's not a pond, everyone moves throwing their arms and legs. Going from this side to that, they hang a medal around their neck.

riddle_original: সুতো টেনে ধরি আমি, বাঁকা আমার গায়। নিশানা ঠিক থাকলে পরে, সোজা ছুটে যায়।
riddle_english: I pull the string back, my body is curved. If the aim is right, it shoots straight ahead.

riddle_original: সবুজ মাঠে লাল সূর্য, ওঠে প্রতিদিন। দেশের জন্য জীবন দিল, কত বীর স্বাধীন।
riddle_english: A red sun in a green field, rises every day. So many brave heroes gave their lives for the country.

riddle_original: সাতটি স্তম্ভ মাথা উঁচু, সাভারে তার বাস। একাত্তরের বীর শহীদদের, সে যে ইতিহাস।
riddle_english: Seven pillars with heads held high, residing in Savar. It is the history of the brave martyrs of '71.

riddle_original: একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারিতে সবাই, ফুল দেয় তার পায়। ভাষার জন্য যারা দিল প্রাণ, তাদের কথা শোনায়।
riddle_english: On the 21st of February, everyone lays flowers at its feet. It tells the story of those who gave their lives for the language.

riddle_original: রুপোলি আঁশ গায় তার, জলের মাঝে ভাসে। জাতীয় মাছ নাম তার, বাঙালি ভালোবাসে।
riddle_english: Silvery scales on its body, it floats in the water. It is the national fish, loved by Bengalis.

riddle_original: সাদা-কালো পালক আমার, মিষ্টি সুরে গাই। দেশের আমি জাতীয় পাখি, সবখানেতে যাই।
riddle_english: Black and white feathers, I sing in a sweet tune. I am the national bird of the country, I go everywhere.

riddle_original: জলের বুকে জন্ম আমার, সাদা রঙের গায়। দেশের আমি জাতীয় ফুল, সবাই ভালোবাসে তায়।
riddle_english: Born in the heart of water, my body is white. I am the national flower of the country, loved by all.

riddle_original: হলুদ গায়ে কালো ডোরা, বনের রাজা ভাই। গর্জে উঠে কাঁপাই সব, জাতীয় পশু তাই।
riddle_english: Black stripes on a golden body, I'm the king of the forest, brother. I roar and make everything tremble, and so I'm the national animal.

riddle_original: গ্রীষ্মকালে রসাল ফল, ঝোলে আমার গায়। শীতল ছায়ায় জুড়াই প্রাণ, জাতীয় গাছ তায়।
riddle_english: In summertime juicy fruit hangs from my body. With cool shade I soothe and refresh you, and so I'm the national tree.

riddle_original: এক দমে ছুটে গিয়ে, ছুঁয়ে আসি ফিরে। জাতীয় খেলা নাম মোর, খেলি মাঠ ঘিরে।
riddle_english: Dashing off in a single breath, I touch and run back. My name is the national game, played all across the field.

riddle_original: নদীর বুকে গভীর বন, সুন্দরী গাছে ভরা। বাঘ মামার বাস এখানে, বিশ্ব-ঐতিহ্য ধরা।
riddle_english: On the breast of the rivers, a deep forest full of sundari trees. Uncle Tiger makes his home here, recognized as world heritage.

riddle_original: গায়ে আমার কাঁটা কাঁটা, ভেতরে কোষ ভারী। দেশের আমি জাতীয় ফল, খেতে মজা ভারি।
riddle_english: My body is spiky, inside the pods are heavy. I am the national fruit of the country, very delicious to eat.

riddle_original: হাঁ আছে, হউ নাই। মাথা আছে, মগজ নাই।
সুতোয় বাঁধা থাকে সে, আকাশেতে ওড়ে। ডানা নেই তবুও সে, সবার মন কাড়ে।
riddle_english: Tied with string, it flies in the sky. It has no wings, yet it captures everyone's heart

riddle_original: হাত নেই, পা নেই, তবুও সে লাফায়। মাঠে ঘাটে শিশুরা, তাকে নিয়ে খেলায়।
riddle_english: No hands, no feet, yet it jumps. Children play with it in the field and grass.

riddle_original: পেন্সিলের ভুলগুলো, আমি দিই মুছে। যতই কাজ করি আমি, শরীর যায় ঘুচে।
riddle_english: I erase the mistakes of pencils. The more I work, the more my body disappears.

riddle_original: রোজ সকালে আমার পেটে, বই খাতা সব ঢোকে। পিঠে চেপে রোজ আমি, যাই যে তোমার সাথে।
riddle_english: Every morning, books and notebooks crowd my belly. I ride on your back every day, going wherever you go.

riddle_original: ছোট ছোট গোল গোল, কাঁচের তৈরি ভাই। আঙুলের টোকায় তারা, ছুটে ছুটে যায়।
riddle_english: Small and round, made of glass. Flicked by fingers, they dart away.

riddle_original: উপরে যাই, নিচে আসি, মাটি ছুঁতে মানা। হাওয়ায় ভেসে উড়তে থাকি, নেইকো আমার ডানা।
riddle_english: I go up, I come down, touching the ground then rising again. I float and fly in the air, I have no fixed place.

riddle_original: রোদ বৃষ্টি মাথার পরে, আগলে রাখি আমি। খুললে যেন ফোটা ফুল, গুটিয়ে গেলে থামি।
riddle_english: In sun and rain, above your head, I shield and keep you safe. Opened up, I'm like a flower in bloom; folded away, I rest.

riddle_original: হাত আছে পা নেই, তবু সারাক্ষণ চলি। সময় হলে ঢং ঢং, ক'টা বাজে বলি।
riddle_english: I have hands but no feet, yet I run all the time. When the hour comes, ding-ding, I tell you what o'clock it is.

riddle_original: পেট আছে পিঠ নেই, মুখ আছে জিভ নেই।
riddle_english: It has a belly but no back, it has a mouth but no tongue.

riddle_original: ধলা মিয়া হাঁটে যায়, নিত্য হাঁটে চিমটা খায়।
riddle_english:
Dhola Mia goes to market,
every day he gets pinched at the market.

riddle_original: হাঁটু জলে ফোটে ফুল, জল শুকাইলে  ফোটে ফুল।
riddle_english: Flowers bloom in knee-deep water, flowers bloom when the water dries up.

riddle_original: আছাড়ে হইনা কাবু, নহি আমরা ফুলবাবু।  টেপাটেপিতে মরণ দশা, আসলে আমি নই মশা।
riddle_english:
We don’t give in just from a slam, we’re no delicate gentlemen.
When things get all squeezed and crushed, I’m in a dying state, but truth is, I’m no mosquito.

riddle_original: তিন অক্ষরে নাম তার রান্না হয় ঘরে, প্রথম অক্ষর বাদ দিলে মেয়ে লোকে পরে।
riddle_english: The three-letter name is used in cooking at home, and if you omit the first letter, it is used by girls.

riddle_original: রাজার বাড়ীর হাতি, নিত্য খায় লাথি ।
riddle_english: The elephant in the king's house is always getting kicked.

riddle_original: হাত আছে পা নাই , মাথা তার কাটা । আস্ত মানুষ গিলে খায় , বুক তার ফাটা।
riddle_english: It has arms but no legs, its head is cut off. It swallows people whole, its chest is cracked.

riddle_original: কে সকালে মাথা হারায়, কিন্তু রাত হলেই টা ফিরে পায়?
riddle_english: Who loses their head in the morning, but regains it at night?

riddle_original: এক ঘরে এক থাম। বল কি তার নাম।
riddle_english: One pillar in one room. Tell me what is its name?

riddle_original: এক ছাগলের তিন মাথা, খায় লতা-পাতা
riddle_english: A goat has three heads, eats vines and leaves

riddle_original: কও চাই কি নাম ধরে আনা মেঘে পানি ঝরে।
riddle_english: Who wants to bring water to the clouds by name?

riddle_original: এক উঠানে দুই ভাই। কেউ না কারে দেখতে পায়।
riddle_english: Two brothers in the same courtyard. Yet they can't see each other.

riddle_original: একটুখানি পুস্কনি, জল টলমল করে।রাজার ছেলের সাধ্য নেই, জাল ফেলতে পারে।
riddle_english: A little pond, the water ripples. The king's son can't afford it, he can cast a net.

riddle_original: পাঁচ বেডা তুইল্যা দিল বত্রিশ বেডার ঘাড়ে। দুয়ারে আছে কুটনা বুড়ী টাইন্যা নেয় ঘরে।
riddle_english:
Five brothers climb up and sit on the necks of thirty‑two brothers;  
an old, toothless woman waits at the door and pulls them all inside the house.

riddle_original: আমি যখন এলাম, তুমি কেনো এলেনা? তুমি যখন এলে, কতো কি খেলে, একবার গেলে, ফিরে তুমি এলে, কিন্তু হায় ! বৃদ্ধকালে আমায় ছেড়ে গেলে!
riddle_english: When I came, why didn't you come? When you came, how much did you play? Once you went, you came back, but alas! You left me in my old age!

riddle_original: আন্ধার ঘরে থাকি আমি নড়াচড়া করি, একটুখানি খাবার পেলে খাবলে তাকে ধরি।
riddle_english: I live in a dark room and move around. Give me a little food and I'll grip it tight.

riddle_original: এক মায়ের পাঁচ সন্তান। কেউ লম্বা, কেউ খাটো, আর একজন বেশ মোটা। একা তারা দুর্বল, কিন্তু একসাথে জড়ালে একেবারে পাথরের মতো শক্ত হয়ে যায়। বল তো কী?
riddle_english: Five children of one mother. Some are tall, some are short, and one is quite stout. Alone they are weak, but when they curl together, they become as hard as a stone. Tell me, what is it?

riddle_original: রাতে ঘরের দুই দরজা বন্ধ থাকে, তবু ভেতরের মানুষটি বহুদূর ঘুরে বেড়ায়। সকালে দরজা দুটো খোলে, কিন্তু মানুষটি আবার ঘরের ভেতরেই আটকা পড়ে যায়। এটা কী?
riddle_english: At night, the two doors of the room remain closed, yet the person inside wanders far and wide. In the morning, the two doors open, but the person gets trapped inside the room again. What is this?

riddle_original: এক পাহাড়ের দুই পাশে দুই ভাই থাকে। তারা সারা পৃথিবী দেখতে পায়, কিন্তু একে অপরকে কখনো দেখতে পায় না। বল তো তারা কারা?
riddle_english: Two brothers live on two sides of a mountain. They can see the whole world, but they can never see each other. Tell me, who are they?

riddle_original: গোল পাহাড়ের চূড়ায় এক ঘন জঙ্গল। প্রতি মাসে গাছ কেটে পরিষ্কার করলেও সেই জঙ্গল কখনো ফুরোয় না। কী সেটা?
riddle_english: A dense forest on top of a round hill. Even if you cut and clear the trees every month, that forest never runs out. What is it?

riddle_original: দুধ সাদা, তুলো সাদা আর সাদা কে? জলে নেমে হেঁটে হেঁটে মাছ খোঁজে যে।
riddle_english: Milk is white, cotton is white, who else is white? It walks into the water step by step, searching for fish.

riddle_original: আমি যাকে মামা বলি, বাবাও বলে তাই। ছেলেও তাকে মামা বলে, মাও বলে তাই।
riddle_english: I call him uncle, my father calls him that too. My son calls him uncle, and so does my mother.

riddle_original: ডালা ভরা সুপারি , গুনতে না পারে বেপারী
riddle_english: The merchant can't count the basket full of betel nuts.

riddle_original: এক গাছে তিন তরকারী, আজব কথা বলি হাড়ি।
riddle_english: From a single tree spring three fine dishes; the cooking pot marvels at this little miracle.

riddle_original: একটু খানি গাছে মারচ ঝুমঝুম করে, একটু  খানি টুকা দিলে  ঝুপঝূপাইয়া পড়ে
riddle_english: A little gust of wind makes the tree sway and jingle; give it a small push, and it comes crashing down with a thud.

riddle_original: ঝি ঝি পাতা ভরা ডাল, ফল বেকা বিচি লাল।
riddle_english: The branches are full of leaves, the fruits are bent and the seeds are red.

riddle_original: মাটির নিচে কাদা, উঠাইলে নবাবজাদা
riddle_english: Mud under the ground, if you lift it up, it will be a prince.

riddle_original: বাড়ির  কাছে কাঠের গাই, বছর বছর দুয়ে খাই।
riddle_english: By the house stands a wooden cow; year after year I milk it and drink.

riddle_original: হাড় মট মট বাকলে দড়ি, তার পাতাতে হয় তরকারী।
riddle_english: The rope is woven from the bones, its leaves are used as a curry.

riddle_original: পেট ভরে না তবু সর্ব প্রাণি খায়, প্রথম অক্ষর বাদ দিলে খেলার নাম হয়।
riddle_english: Even if the stomach is not full, all animals eat, if you leave out the first letter, that's the name of the game.

riddle_original:
ভোটের আগে সবার ঘরে,
ভোটের পরে দূর শহরে।
riddle_english:
Before the vote, at everyone’s door;
After the vote, off in a distant city.

riddle_original:
কাগজে থাকে অনেক নাম,
এক চাপ দিতেই বদলায় দাম।
riddle_english:
Many names sit on paper;
With one stamp, the price of a name changes.

riddle_original:
পাঁচ বছরে একবার আসি,
সবার হাতে শক্তি বসাই।
riddle_english:
Once every five years I come;
I place power in everyone’s hands.

riddle_original:
সিংহাসন নয়, তবু লড়াই ভারী,
যে পায় সে হয় দেশের কর্তা ভারী।
riddle_english:
Not a throne, yet the battle is fierce;
Whoever wins becomes a great ruler of the country.

riddle_original:
লাঠি হাতে হাঁটতাম আমি,
অহিংসাই ছিল বল।
সত্যাগ্রহের পথে হেঁটে,
কাঁপিয়েছি বিদেশি দল।
riddle_english:
I walked with a stick in hand;
Non-violence was my strength.
Walking the path of Satyagraha,
I shook the foreign rulers.

riddle_original:
নামেতে আমি দেশের বন্ধু,
বাংলার গর্ব ভারী।
আইনের মঞ্চ ছেড়ে শেষে,
স্বাধীনতারই সওয়ারি।
riddle_english:
In name, I am the nation’s friend;
A great pride of Bengal.
Leaving the stage of law behind,
I finally rode for freedom.

riddle_original:
“তোমরা আমাকে রক্ত দাও,”
ডাক দিয়েছিলাম প্রাণে।
আজাদ হিন্দের স্বপ্ন বুকে,
চলেছিলাম যুদ্ধগানে।
riddle_english:
“Give me your blood,”
I called out with all my soul.
With the dream of Azad Hind in my heart,
I marched on with songs of war.

riddle_original:
গোলাপ ছিল বুকের কাছে,
শিশুরা ছিল প্রিয়।
স্বাধীন দেশের প্রথম পথে,
স্বপ্ন দেখালাম নিত্য।
riddle_english:
A rose stayed close to my chest;
Children were dear to me.
On independent India’s first path,
I kept showing dreams each day.

riddle_original:
আইনের বই হাতে নিয়ে,
সমতার পথ দেখাই।
সংবিধানের পাতায় পাতায়,
অধিকারের কথা পাই।
riddle_english:
With a law book in hand,
I show the path of equality.
On every page of the Constitution,
I find the words of rights.

riddle_original:
কালো কোটে দাঁড়িয়েছিলাম,
দাসপ্রথার বিরুদ্ধে।
গৃহযুদ্ধের আগুন পেরিয়ে,
স্বাধীনতার সূত্রে।
riddle_english:
In a black coat I stood,
Against the chains of slavery.
Through the fire of civil war,
I moved toward the cause of freedom.

riddle_original:
সিংহাসনে বসে ছিলাম,
বিশ্বজয়ের ছিল স্বপ্ন।
কলিঙ্গ দেখে বদলে গেলাম,
ধর্ম হলো আমার যন্ত্র।
riddle_english:
I sat upon a throne,
With dreams of conquering the world.
After seeing Kalinga, I changed;
Dharma became my guiding tool.

riddle_original:
ইটের শহর, নদীর ধারে,
লিপি আজও রহস্য ভারে।
স্নানঘর আছে, রাস্তা সোজা,
বল দেখি সভ্যতাটা কোন সজা?
riddle_english:
A city of bricks, beside the river;
Its script still weighs with mystery.
It has a great bath, its roads are straight
Tell me, which civilization is this?

riddle_original:
এক রাণী ঘোড়ায় চড়ে,
যুদ্ধ করল প্রাণপণে।
ইংরেজদের চোখে চোখ রেখে,
নাম লিখল ইতিহাসে।
riddle_english:
A queen rode on horseback,
And fought with all her might.
Looking the British straight in the eye,
She wrote her name into history.

riddle_original:
রক্তে রাঙা এক বাগান,
নীরব হলো হাজার প্রাণ।
স্বাধীনতার আগুন জ্বলে,
ভারত কাঁদে সেই অবসানে।
riddle_english:
A garden stained red with blood;
Thousands of lives fell silent.
The fire of freedom burned on,
As India wept at that tragic end.

riddle_original:
মুকুট মাথায় মুঘল রাজা,
শিল্প-সৌন্দর্য যার সাজা।
প্রিয়ার স্মৃতিতে গড়ল ধন,
সাদা পাথরে অমর মন।
riddle_english:
With a crown upon his head, a Mughal king;
Art and beauty were his adornment.
In memory of his beloved, he built a treasure,
An immortal heart in white marble.

riddle_original:
সিপাহির হাতে আগুন জ্বলে,
কার্তুজে ওঠে রাগ।
১৮৫৭-র ঝড়ের ভিতর,
কাঁপে ইংরেজ ভাগ।
riddle_english:
Fire burned in the sepoys’ hands;
Anger rose over the cartridges.
In the storm of 1857,
The British fate began to tremble.

riddle_original:
গঙ্গার ধারে জন্ম আমার,
জ্ঞান আর ধর্মে খ্যাত।
বোধিবৃক্ষের নীচে বসে,
দুঃখের করলাম ব্যাখ্যাত।
riddle_english:
I was born by the Ganges,
Famed for wisdom and faith.
Sitting beneath the Bodhi tree,
I explained the meaning of suffering.

riddle_original: চার পায়ে থাকে স্থির, আট পায়ে চলে পথ।
riddle_english: It stays still on four legs, but moves along the road on eight legs.

riddle_original:
লোহার মানুষ নামটি আমার,
ঐক্যের পথে দিলাম ডাক।
রাজ্য রাজ্য জুড়ে শেষে,
গড়লাম ভারতের একতা-পথ।
riddle_english:
I am known as the Iron Man,
I called for the path of unity.
Joining state after state,
I built India’s road to oneness.

riddle_original:
মুণ্ড কাটা মূর্তি আমার,
ইতিহাসে নামটি রয়।
কুষাণ যুগের রাজা আমি,
বল দেখি কে সে হয়?
riddle_english:
My statue has a severed head,
Yet my name lives on in history.
I am a king of the Kushan age
Tell me, who am I?

riddle_original: তিন অক্ষরের জায়গার নাম, উল্টালেও যা পাল্টায় না।
riddle_english: A three-letter place name that remains the same even when reversed.

riddle_original: তিন অক্ষরের জলাশয়, মাঝের অক্ষর বাদ দিলে গাছের খাদ্য হয়।
riddle_english: A three-letter water body; if the middle letter is removed, it becomes food for plants.

riddle_original: চার অক্ষর নাম আমার, উত্তর ভারতে, শেষ দুই বাদ  দিলে , শুনি তাই পেতে
riddle_english: My name is four letters, from North India, if you drop the last two, you get what you use to hear.

riddle_original: বরফের ঘর আমি, উত্তরে আবাস, আমার-ই জন্য দেশে, বর্ষার আভাস
riddle_english: I am the house of ice, dwelling in the north, I am the one who provides, the first glimpse of the monsoon.

riddle_original: জলের বুকে বন, সুন্দরী গাছ, ডোরা কাটা রাজা, করতে পারো আঁচ ?
riddle_english: Forest in the water, beautiful trees, striped king, can you make a guess?

riddle_original: বাইরে আমি শান্ত যেন, ভিতরে আগুন বাস, রেগে গেলে উড়িয়ে ধোঁয়া, করাই সর্বনাশ
riddle_english: I may seem calm on the outside, but inside me lives fire. When I get angry, I blow smoke and cause destruction.

riddle_original: কালো মেঘে ঢাকি আকাশ, বজ্রপাত  আর বারি , আমায় দেখে চাষির মুখে, হাসি ফোটে ভারি
riddle_english: I cover the sky is with black clouds, lightning and rain, a smile spreads on the farmer's face when he sees me.

riddle_original: চায়ের বাগান পাহাড় ঘেরা, ঠান্ডা হাওয়ার দেশ, দূর থেকে কাঞ্চনজঙ্ঘা, দেখতে লাগে বেশ
riddle_english: The tea gardens are surrounded by mountains, the land of cool breezes, Kanchenjunga from a distance, looks quite beautiful.

riddle_original: সাদা সাদা উঠি দুলে, নদীর ধারের ঘাস, আমায় দেখেই বাঙালির মন, পুজোর পায় আভাস।
riddle_english: I rise white and sway, the grass by the riverbank, the Bengali's mind, upon seeing me, gets a glimpse of the puja.

riddle_original: হলুদ ট্যাক্সি চলছে ছুটে,  ভিড় জমেছে পথে, বইমেলাতে হারিয়ে গেলাম,  আড্ডা আর গল্পেতে
riddle_english: The yellow taxi is rushing by, the crowd is gathering on the road, I got lost in the book fair, chatting and talking.

riddle_original:
কাঁধে আসে কাঁধে যায় বিনা দোষে মার খায় 
পূজা-পার্বণে ডাক পড়ে,
ধুমধাম আমার জীবন।

আমার গলা নেই, তবু গান গাই,
তার ছুঁলেই সুর ভেসে যায়।
riddle_english:
I have no throat, yet I sing;
Touch my strings, and melodies float away.

riddle_original:
দুই হাতে বাজাই আমায়,
তালে তালে নাচে মন।
ধুমধাম আমার জীবন।

সাদা-কালো দাঁত আছে,
কামড়ায় না কখনো।
আঙুল ছুঁলেই গান শোনায়,
ঘর ভরে যায় সুরে।
riddle_english:
It has black and white teeth,
But it never bites.
Touch it with your fingers,
And it fills the room with music.

riddle_original:
লাল-নীল-সবুজ মিলে,
ক্যানভাসে করি খেলা।
আমায় ছাড়া ছবি হলে,
থাকে ফাঁকা মেলা।
riddle_english:
Red, blue, and green together,
I play upon the canvas.
Without me, a picture would feel
Like an empty fair.

riddle_original:
বাঁশের দেহ, ফাঁপা বুক,
শ্বাস পেলেই গান।
কৃষ্ণের হাতে বিখ্যাত আমি,
সুরে ভরে প্রাণ।
riddle_english:
A bamboo body, a hollow chest;
With breath, I begin to sing.
Famous in Krishna’s hands,
I fill the soul with melody.

riddle_original:
শরীর আমার কাঠের,
পেটের ভেতর তার।
ধনুক ছুঁলেই কেঁদে উঠি,
সুরের অপার ধার।
riddle_english:
My body is made of wood,
With strings inside my belly.
When the bow touches me, I cry out,
Pouring an endless stream of melody.

riddle_original:
মাটির দেহ, রঙিন সাজ,
কুমোরপাড়ায় জন্ম।
পূজার ঘরে বসে আমি,
ভক্তির করি কর্ম।
riddle_english:
A body made of clay, dressed in colors,
Born in the potter’s quarter.
I sit in the worship room,
Doing the work of devotion.

riddle_original:
কাপড় জুড়ে গল্প বলি,
রঙে ভরা গান।
গ্রামের শিল্প হাতে ধরে,
বাংলার ঐতিহ্য মান।
riddle_english:
I tell stories across cloth,
A song filled with color.
Held in the hands of village art,
I carry Bengal’s tradition.

riddle_original:
লম্বা পটে গল্প আঁকি,
রঙে রঙে গান।
মনসামঙ্গল, রাজা-রানী,
গুটিয়ে রাখি প্রাণ।
riddle_english:
On a long scroll, I paint stories;
In color after color, I sing.
Manasa Mangal, kings and queens
I roll them up and keep their spirit within.

riddle_original:
গোল গোল আমি, মাঠে করি দৌড়,
পায়ে ঠেলা খেয়ে করি সবার জোড়।
riddle_english:
Round and round I am, running across the field;
Kicked by feet, I bring everyone together.

riddle_original:
ব্যাট আছে, বল আছে,
উইকেট আমার ঘর।
ছয় মারলে সবাই চিৎকার করে,
বলে - কী সুন্দর শট!
riddle_english:
There is a bat, there is a ball;
The wicket is my home.
When someone hits a six, everyone shouts,
“What a beautiful shot!”

riddle_original:
র‍্যাকেট হাতে দাঁড়াই আমি,
জালের ওপারে সাথী।
ছোট্ট বল উড়ে যায়,
জিতলে মুখে হাসি।
riddle_english:
I stand with a racket in hand,
My partner across the net.
A little ball flies through the air;
When I win, a smile comes to my face.

riddle_original:
বোর্ডের ওপর ঘুঁটি চলে,
রাজা থাকে মাঝখানে।
যুদ্ধ হয় বুদ্ধির জোরে,
মাঠ লাগে না তাতে।
সবাই তাকে লাথি মারে, তবু মাঠে তারই সম্মান।
riddle_english: Everyone kicks it, yet it is honored on the field.

riddle_original: তিন অক্ষরের ভদ্রলোক; প্রথম অক্ষর গেলে দেশের নাম।
riddle_english: A three-letter gentleman; remove the first letter and it becomes a country’s name.

riddle_original:
এক পায়ে লাফিয়ে চলি,
ঘরে ঘরে দাগ।
ছুঁয়ে দিলে ধরা পড়ি,
হাসিতে ভরে ভাগ।
riddle_english:
I hop along on one foot,
Across squares drawn on the ground.
Touch me, and I’m caught;
Laughter fills the game all around.

riddle_original:
এক কথায় ছুঁয়ে পালাই,
শ্বাস ধরে করি দৌড়।
মাঠের মাঝে লাইন টানা,
ধরা পড়লে ভীষণ জোর।
riddle_english:
I say one word and run to tag,
Holding my breath as I race.
Lines are drawn across the field,
If I’m caught, it becomes a fierce chase.

riddle_original:
খালি পায়ে মাঠে নেমে,
ইংরেজদের দিলাম টক্কর।
বাংলার ফুটবলের গর্ব আমি,
সাহসে ভরা আমার কণ্ঠস্বর।
riddle_english:
Barefoot, I stepped onto the field,
And challenged the British side.
I am Bengal’s football pride,
With courage as my guide.

riddle_original:
হলুদ-সবুজ এক পাশে,
লাল-মেরুন আরেক দল।
ডার্বির দিনে মাঠ কাঁপে,
পায়ে পায়ে ঘোরে বল।
riddle_english:
Yellow and green on one side,
Red and maroon on the other team.
On derby day, the field shakes,
As the ball rolls from foot to foot.

riddle_original:
তাজের মতো সাদা নই,
তবু আমিই দিল্লির গর্ব।
লাল পাথরের বুকের ভেতর,
সম্রাটদের ছিল সর্বস্ব।
riddle_english:
I am not white like the Taj,
Yet I am Delhi’s pride.
Within my chest of red stone,
Lay the emperors’ entire world.

riddle_original:
আমি কোনো রাজা নই,
তবু রাজাদেরও শাসাই।
আইনের পাতায় দেশ চালিয়ে,
জনতার অধিকার বাসাই।
riddle_english:
I am no king,
Yet I rule even the rulers.
Through the pages of law, I run the nation,
And give people’s rights a home.

riddle_original: প্রেমের স্মৃতি হয়ে দাঁড়িয়ে আছে তার নাম; শেষ অংশ বাদ দিলে থাকে অমূল্য ধন।
riddle_english: Its name stands as a memory of love; remove the last part and a priceless treasure remains.

riddle_original: হাজার খানা জিনিসের, সবকটা নয় সত্যি, নবাবদের স্মৃতি বুকে,  দাঁড়িয়ে আছি দিব্যি

চাকার মাঝে চব্বিশ দাগ,
নীল রঙে গর্ব ভারী।
তিন রঙের বুকের মাঝে,
দেশের মান রাখি।
riddle_english:
Twenty-four spokes inside a wheel,
Proud and deep in blue.
At the heart of three colors,
I uphold the nation’s honor.

riddle_original:
সিংহ চারটি পিঠে পিঠ,
সত্যের পথে ডাক।
সরকারি কাগজ, মুদ্রার বুকে,
আমার থাকে ছাপ।
riddle_english:
Four lions standing back to back,
Calling us to the path of truth.
On government papers and coins,
My mark is always seen.

riddle_original:
সমুদ্র পাড়ে রথের চাকা,
পাথরে বাঁধা গান।
সূর্যের ঘরে সময় থামে,
শিল্পে জাগে প্রাণ।
riddle_english:
By the seashore, a chariot wheel,
A song bound in stone.
In the house of the Sun, time stands still,
And art awakens the soul.

riddle_original:
সূর্য দেখে সময় বলি,
পাথরে বাঁধা জ্ঞান।
আকাশ মাপি ছায়ার পথে,
বিজ্ঞানের সম্মান।
riddle_english:
By watching the Sun, I tell the time,
Knowledge bound in stone.
I measure the sky through shadows,
A proud monument of science.

riddle_original:
হাওয়ার ওপর দাঁড়িয়ে যেন,
গোলাপি শহরের সাজ।
জানালায় জানালায় গল্প বলে,
রাজরানীর লাজ।
riddle_english:
As if standing upon the wind,
It adorns the Pink City.
Window after window tells stories
Of royal queens in modesty.

riddle_original:
নয় চূড়া মাথায় নিয়ে,
টেরাকোটার গায়ে গান।
মন্দিরের দেয়াল জুড়ে,
বাংলার শিল্পের মান।
riddle_english:
With nine towers on my head,
My terracotta walls sing.
Across the temple walls,
I carry the pride of Bengal’s art.

riddle_original: কাজ করতে করতে থেমে যায়, মাথা ছাঁটলেই আবার শুরু হয়।
riddle_english: It stops while working; trim its head and it starts again.

riddle_original: কুমির এলো জলের ধারে, কে নামবে সাহস করে , জলে বিপদ ডাঙ্গা বাঁচায় , ছোটবেলায় খেলেছে সবাই
riddle_english: The crocodile came to the water's edge, who would dare to get in? The danger is in the water, but the shore is safe, everyone played this game in their childhood.

riddle_original: চোখদুটো যেই বন্ধ করে, গুনতে শুরু করি, একনিমেষে লুকিয়ে পড়তে, কেউ করেনা  দেরি
riddle_english: As soon as I close my eyes, no one delays to hide instantly

riddle_original: চোখদুটো বেঁধে, ঘোরে  ধীরে ধীরে, যেই কাউকে ধরে , সে-ই এবার ফেরে
riddle_english: Blindfolded, slowly spinning, whomever gets caught, has to returns

riddle_original: ছোট্ট ছোট্ট রঙিন গোলা, পকেট ভরা সুখ, হারলে মনটা খারাপ লাগে, জিতলে হাসি মুখ
riddle_english: Small colorful balls, pocket full of happiness, feeling sad when you lose, smiling when you win

riddle_original: কি এমন জিনিস বলে ফেলো ভাই, পরিষ্কার করলে কালো হয় তাই?
riddle_english: What kind of thing is that, brother, that turns black when you clean it?

riddle_original: ডানা নেই তবুও আমি উড়ি ঘরের মাঝে, ছোট্ট হাতের এক ঠেলাতেই চলি নিজের সাজে।
riddle_english: Even though I don't have wings, I still fly around the house, moving in my own way with a push of a kid's hand

riddle_original: গল্প বলে বাড়াই রঙ, আড্ডা জমাই বেশ, পটলডাঙার নাম শুনলেই, চিনবে আমায় শেষ
riddle_english: I add color by telling stories, I gather a lot of chatter, just by hearing the name of Pataldanga, you will instantly recognize me.

riddle_original: আমরা দুজন আর সুপারিন্টেন্ডেন্ট, ছোট্ট বড় সকলের ফেন্ড !
riddle_english: The two of us and the superintendent, friends of all, children and adults!

riddle_original: পাঁচজনের-ই দল আমাদের, সঙ্গে পঞ্চু আছে, রহস্য দেখলেই ছুটে যাই, সাহস বুকের মাঝে
riddle_english: We are a group of five, with Panchu with us, we run when we see a mystery, courage is in our hearts

riddle_original:
ঘরের মাথার ওপরে থাকি,
শীতকালে চুপটি মেরে।
গ্রীষ্ম এলে ঘুরতে থাকি,
প্রাণ জুড়াই হাওয়া করে।
riddle_english:
I stay above the head inside the room,
Silent through the winter days.
When summer comes, I start to spin,
Cooling life with my breeze.

riddle_original: আমার মধ্যে আছো তুমি তোমার মধ্যে নাই,আমাদের মধ্যে যাচ্ছ তুমি বাবার মধ্যে নাই
riddle_english:
You are inside me,
But not inside yourself.
You pass through us,
But not through father.

riddle_original: জলে জন্ম, জলে বাস; জলের সঙ্গেই তার সর্বনাশ।
riddle_english: Born in water, lives in water; water itself causes its destruction.

riddle_original: তিন অক্ষরের সুখের নাম; প্রথমটি গেলে বনে তার স্থান।
riddle_english: A three-letter name for comfort; remove the first letter and it belongs in the forest.

riddle_original: নামে আছে দ্বীপের ছাপ, তবু বসতি নেই কোথাও; আলো দিয়ে যায় নিরন্তর।
riddle_english: Its name carries the mark of an island, yet it has no settlement; it keeps giving light.

riddle_original: কখনো সে প্রাণঘাতী, কখনো সে জীবনধারণের সাথী।
riddle_english: Sometimes it is deadly, sometimes it is a companion for survival.

riddle_original: যত টানো, তত কমে; শেষে শুধু ছাই হয়ে থামে।
riddle_english: The more you pull from it, the shorter it gets; in the end, it stops as ash.

riddle_original: তেল ছাড়াই আলো জ্বালে, আলো দিতে দিতে নিজেই ক্ষয়ে যায়।
riddle_english: It gives light without oil, and wears itself away while giving light.

riddle_original: ব্যাংক হলেও মুদ্রা রাখে না, রাখে জীবন বাঁচানোর ভরসা।
riddle_english: Though it is a bank, it does not store money; it stores hope for saving lives.

riddle_original: আগুনে নরম, ঠান্ডায় কঠিন; আলো দিতেও সে আপনজন।
riddle_english: Soft in fire, hard in the cold; it is also a friend in giving light.

riddle_original:
মাটির নিচে থাকে বুড়ি,
কাপড় পরে তিন কুড়ি।
ধোপায় কাপড় নেয় না,
তবুও কাপড় ময়লা হয় না।
riddle_english:
An old woman lives under the ground,
Wearing sixty layers of clothes.
The washerman never takes her clothes,
Yet her clothes never get dirty.

riddle_original: কোন জিনিস গাছে সবুজ দোকানে কালো , বাড়িতে লাল ?
riddle_english:
What thing is green on the tree,
black in the shop,
and red at home?

riddle_original:
আকাশ থেকে নামল বুড়ি, কাঁথা-কম্বল লইয়া,
সেই বুড়ি কাঁথা খায় নীরবে বসিয়া।
riddle_english:
An old woman came down from the sky,
Carrying quilts and blankets.
That old woman eats the quilts,
Sitting silently.

riddle_original: জীবনে একবারই ফল ধরে; তবু ঘরে ঘরে তার কদর।
riddle_english: It bears fruit only once in its life; yet it is valued in every home.
human_answer_comment: Not that common for bamboo to bear fruit

riddle_original: পথে-ঘাটে ঘুরে বেড়ায়, ছয় পায়ে চলে সারি বেঁধে।
riddle_english: It wanders along roads and paths, walking in lines on six legs.

riddle_original: গাছের মাথায় ঝুলে থাকে, ভিতরে তার নোনা-মিঠে জল।
riddle_english: It hangs at the top of a tree; inside it has sweet-salty water.

riddle_original: কান আছে হাঁটুর কাছে, তবু চারদিকের শব্দ পায়।
riddle_english: Its ears are near its knees, yet it hears sounds from all around.

riddle_original: পাতা খাই, ফুলও খাই, ফলও যায় পাতে - বল তো কোন গাছ?
riddle_english: We eat its leaves, flowers, and fruits too - tell me, which tree is it?

riddle_original: আকাশে ভাসে ডানা ছাড়া, শব্দ করে মুখ ছাড়া; বিদ্যুতে তার বুক চিরে যায়।
riddle_english: It floats in the sky without wings, makes sound without a mouth; lightning tears through its chest.

riddle_original: জলে জন্ম, ডাঙাতেও বাস; ফুল বললেই সবার মনে তার ধ্যান।
riddle_english: Born in water, lives on land too; when one says flower, everyone thinks of it.

riddle_original:
বত্রিশ ভাই এক ঘরে রয়,
সাদা কাপড় পরে সবাই দাঁড়ায়।
riddle_english:
Thirty-two brothers live in one house,
All stand wearing white clothes.

riddle_original:
লাল ঘরের মধ্যে সাদা সাদা সারি,
খাবার এলে কাটে তারা ভারি।
riddle_english:
Inside a red house, white rows stand,
When food arrives, they cut it with force.

riddle_original:
দরজা আছে, তালা নেই,
খোলে-বন্ধ হয় সারাক্ষণ।
riddle_english:
It has a door, but no lock;
It opens and closes all the time.

riddle_original:
জন্ম থেকে সঙ্গে থাকে,
কিন্তু সামনে থাকলেও দেখা যায় না।
riddle_english:
It stays with you from birth,
But even when it is in front, you cannot see it.

riddle_original:
হাড় নেই, দাঁত নেই,
তবু কথা বলে অবিরাম।
riddle_english:
It has no bones, no teeth,
Yet it speaks without end.

riddle_original:
নীরবে চলে দিনরাত,
থামলেই শেষ সব কথা।
riddle_english:
It works silently day and night;
If it stops, all words come to an end.

riddle_original:
দুই স্তম্ভে দাঁড়ায় মানুষ,
চলতে গেলে লাগে তাদেরই সহায়।
riddle_english:
A person stands on two pillars;
To walk, they need their support.

riddle_original:
মাথায় থাকে কালো বন,
কাটলে আবার হয় জন্ম।
riddle_english:
A black forest stays on the head;
Cut it, and it grows again.

riddle_original:
দশ ভাই একসঙ্গে থাকে,
কাজে গেলে সবাই নামে।
riddle_english:
Ten brothers live together;
When it’s time to work, they all come down.

riddle_original: দুই ভাই পাশাপাশি থাকে; একজন এলে আরেকজন যায়।
riddle_english: The two stay side by side; when one comes, the other goes.

riddle_original:
Sou gaúcho, fui militar,
advogado, político
e até ditador.
Criei a CLT.
Sai da vida,
Para entrar na história.
Ainda hoje, por alguns,
sou lembrado.
riddle_english:
I was born in the South of Brazil
I was a soldier, a politician,
And even a dictator.
I created the brazilian labor laws.
I left this life
To enter history.
Even today, by some,
I am remembered.
riddle_note:
Getúlio vargas
foi o presidente que
mais tempo governou
o Brasil,
somando suas
duas passagens
no governo.
Fez muitas mudanças,
marcantes no Brasil.

riddle_original:
Sou o nome de um animal do mar,
mas também de uma figura nacional.
Já passei pelo movimento sindical
e cheguei ao cargo mais alto do Planalto.
riddle_english:
I am the name of a sea animal,
but also of a national figure.
I was once part of the labor union movement
and reached the highest office in the Planalto.
riddle_note: Referência ao líder sindical que se tornou presidente da república e que possui o nome associado a um animal.

riddle_original: Meu nome parece serviço de carro, mas marcou a política brasileira. O que sou?
riddle_english: My name sounds like a car service, but I left a major mark on Brazilian politics. What am I?
riddle_note: "Lava Jato" means something like “car wash” or “jet wash” in Portuguese, but in Brazil it became famous as the name of a major corruption investigation that strongly affected national politics.

riddle_original: Fui palhaço antes de virar deputado, e meu slogan prometia que pior não ficava. Quem sou eu?
riddle_english: I was a clown before becoming a congressman, and my campaign slogan promised that things couldn’t get any worse. Who am I?
riddle_note: Tiririca is a Brazilian comedian and clown who later became a federal deputy. His famous campaign slogan was "It can’t get any worse than this.”

riddle_original: Meu apelido veio dos dentes, mas meu nome ficou ligado à liberdade. Quem sou?
riddle_english: My nickname came from teeth, but my name became tied to freedom. Who am I?
riddle_note: “Tiradentes” means something like “tooth-puller” in Portuguese, referring to his work as a dentist. He later became a symbol of a movement associated with independence in Brazil.

riddle_original: Fui eleito para conduzir uma nova era no Brasil. Mas antes da posse, parti deixando perguntas que muitos ainda tentam responder. Quem sou eu?
riddle_english:
I was elected to lead a new era in Brazil.
But before taking office, I passed away, leaving questions that many still try to answer.
Who am I?

riddle_original:
Fui a mulher que quebrou uma barreira histórica ao alcançar o posto mais alto do país.
Mas minha permanência nele terminou antes do fim.
riddle_english:
I was the woman who broke a historic barrier by reaching the highest office in my country.
But my time there ended before it was supposed to.

riddle_original:
Quando construí Brasília,
Me chamaram de louco por utopia
Mas tudo que eu queria
Era "50 anos em 5".
Quem sou eu?
riddle_english:
When I built Brasília,
They called me crazy for a utopia
But all that I wanted
Was "50 years in 5".
Who am I?

riddle_original:
Forças ocultas ao meu redor
Carta renúncia na ponta da linha
Contra a corrupção pro povo ver
"Varre, varre, varre vassourinha!"
Quem sou eu?
riddle_english:
Hidden forces around me
Resignation letter at the end of the line
Against corruption for the people to see
"Sweep, sweep, sweep, little broom!"
Who am I?

riddle_original:
Seu dinheiro preso na poupança,
Um choque que o Brasil não esquece jamais.
O Fiat Elba foi a minha lambança,
Fui eleito o Caçador de Marajás.
Quem sou eu?
riddle_english:
Your money trapped in the savings account,
A shock that Brazil never forgets.
The Fiat Elba was my mess,
I was elected the Hunter of Maharajas.
Who am I?

riddle_original:
Para alguns fomos heróis,
Para outros, vilões
Desbravamos o Brasil.
Nas rodovias,
somos homenageados.
Somos do Período Colonial
E muito ouro e prata,
buscamos no interior.
riddle_english:
To some, we were heroes,
To others, villains.
We ventured across Brazil.
On the highways,
We are honored.
We are from the Colonial Period,
And much gold and silver
We sought in the countryside.
riddle_note:
Os bandeirantes são
muito controversos,
alguns os amam pela
interiorização do
Brasil,
outros os odeiam
por seus
conflitos.

riddle_original: Sou lembrado no tanque do carro e na história da Independência. Quem sou?
riddle_english: I am remembered both at the car’s fuel tank and in the history of Brazil’s Independence. Who am I?
riddle_note: Ipiranga is associated both with Brazilian gas stations and with the Ipiranga stream, where a symbolic moment in Brazil’s Independence took place.

riddle_original: Meu apelido lembra luz, mas minha história passou pelo sertão. Entre cangaceiros e batalhas, meu nome virou lenda.
riddle_english:
My nickname is linked to light, but my story was written in the backlands.
Among cangaceiros and battles, my name became legend.
riddle_note: Lampião was the nickname of Virgulino Ferreira da Silva, the most famous leader of the cangaço, a social and armed movement that took place in Brazil's northeastern backlands during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. His nickname, "Lampião," is associated with light, which is why the riddle mentions it. He led groups of cangaceiros who traveled across the sertão (the Brazilian backlands), becoming one of the most iconic and controversial figures in Brazilian history.

riddle_original:
Entre o barbeiro e o coração, encontrei uma descoberta que mudou a medicina.
Meu nome ficou tão ligado a ela que hoje os dois são lembrados juntos.
Quem sou eu?
riddle_english:
Between the kissing bug and the heart, I made a discovery that changed medicine.
My name became so closely linked to it that the two are remembered together.
Who am I?
riddle_note: This riddle refers to Carlos Chagas, the Brazilian physician who discovered Chagas disease. The phrase "kissing bug" refers to the insect commonly known in Brazil as the barbeiro, which can transmit the parasite responsible for the disease. The reference to the heart comes from the fact that Chagas disease can cause serious cardiac complications.

riddle_original:
Refúgio dos sertanejos
Terra prometida pelo Conselheiro
A nova República não poupou a violência
Massacre, fogo e morteiro
O que sou eu?
riddle_english:
Refuge of the backlanders
Promised land by the Counselor
The new Republic did not spare violence
Massacre, fire, and mortar
What am I?

riddle_original:
Café, inovação e industrialização
Um respiro aos trabalhistas
Centralização, Estado Novo, perseguição
Pesadelo dos comunistas
A que período me refiro?
riddle_english:
Coffee, innovation and industrialization
A breath of relief for the labor workers
Centralization, New State, persecution
Nightmare of the communists
What period am I referring to?

riddle_original:
Fui regente do império e "Redentora",
Uma lei fundamental eu assinei
Recusei virar uma estátua protetora
Para sempre marcada na história ficarei
Quem sou eu?
riddle_english:
I was regent of the empire and "Redeemer",
A fundamental law I signed
I refused to become a protective statue
Forever marked in history I will remain
Who am I?

riddle_original:
É para o bem de todos
À Coroa depois me explico
Para a felicidade da Nação
Digam ao povo que eu fico!
Que evento foi esse?
riddle_english:
It is for the good of all
To the Crown later I will explain myself
For the happiness of the Nation
Tell the people that I stay!
What event was this?
riddle_note: The translation "I Stay Day" is literal but the event is commonly referred to in the original Portuguese name "Dia do Fico".

riddle_original:
Por causa de uma epidemia
A vacinação foi compulsória
O governo invadiu lares
E Oswaldo Cruz fez história
Que evento foi esse?
riddle_english:
Because of an epidemic
Vaccination was compulsory
The government invaded homes
And Oswaldo Cruz was marked in history
What event was this?

riddle_original:
"Na minha época que era bom", dizem eles
Mas muita gente foi forçada a ir embora
Perseguição e tortura, apesar do "milagre"
Um dos períodos mais tristes de nossa história...
riddle_english:
"In my time it was good," they say
But many people were sent away
Persecution and torture, despite the "miracle"
One of the saddest periods of our history...

riddle_original:
Tenho nome composto por doença
e por estilo musical, 
acompanho a bacia de um grande
rio,
fui palco de guerra no começo da
república.
riddle_english:
I have a name composed of
a disease
and a musical style,
I follow the basin of a great river,
I was the stage of a war at the
beginning of the Republic
riddle_note:
Depressão sertaneja,
onde aconteceu
Canudos,
é uma parte 
importante
do relevo brasileiro

riddle_original: Tenho nome bíblico, mas sou porta de entrada da Amazônia. Quem sou?
riddle_english: I have a biblical name, but I am known as a gateway to the Amazon. Who am I?
riddle_note: Belém is the Portuguese name for Bethlehem, a biblical place name. In Brazil, Belém is also the capital of Pará - one of the biggest cities of the Amazon region

riddle_original:
Com as mãos abertas, encaro a Cidade Maravilhosa.
Entre o céu e o mar, sou fé em forma grandiosa.
riddle_english:
With open hands, I face the Marvelous City.
Between sky and sea, I am faith in a grand form.

riddle_original:
Entre montanhas e pastagens
Onde o Velho Chico brota da terra
Lar do melhor queijo do mundo, eu acho
Esconde-se essa importante serra
riddle_english:
Between mountains and pastures
Where the Velho Chico springs from the earth
Home of the best cheese in the world, I think
Hides this important mountain range

riddle_original:
Um grande tesouro nacional
Onde a onça e o tuiuiú têm sua morada
Sofre e arde com as queimadas
A nossa maior planície alagada
Que bioma é esse?
riddle_english:
A great national treasure
Where the jaguar and the jabiru have their home
Suffers and burns with the fires
Our largest flooded plain
What biome is this?

riddle_original:
A maior metrópole das Américas
Gigante cidade global
Seu nome remete a um apóstolo
Nossa selva de pedra tropical
riddle_english:
The largest metropolis of the Americas
Giant global city
Its name refers to an apostle
Our tropical stone jungle

riddle_original:
Nasci planejada, fico no centro e 
sou a casa de muitos tomadores de 
decisão do país.
riddle_english:
I was born planned, I am located in 
the center, and I am home to many of 
the country’s decision-makers.

riddle_original:
Estou perto de três fronteiras.
Sobre mim, muita água e cachoeiras.
riddle_english:
I stand near three borders.
Around me, water falls with great force.

riddle_original:
Árvores tortas de casca dura
Ameaçadas pela agricultura
Biodiversidade incomparável
O lobo-guará é invejável
Que bioma sou eu?
riddle_english:
Twisted trees of hard bark
Threatened by agriculture
Incomparable biodiversity
The maned wolf is enviable
What biome am I?

riddle_original:
Forte cultura afro-brasileira
Arquitetura de herança colonial
Os tambores do Olodum aqui ecoam
Na nossa mais antiga capital
Que cidade sou eu?
riddle_english:
Strong Afro-Brazilian culture
Architecture of colonial heritage
The drums of Olodum echo here
